notes:
Account summary
- Payments company; two initial LLM workstreams: (1) fraud ops triage/copilot for analysts, (2) customer support assistant for escalations.
- Strong preference for regulated posture: "We can’t send transaction details to a public endpoint." Open to VPC-based approach; on-prem not required today.

Key stakeholders (known)
- Primary champion: Director, Fraud Operations (name redacted in notes; engaged, technical).
- Technical owner: Platform Engineering Manager (owns internal API gateway + observability).
- Security: Security Engineering lead + GRC analyst will run questionnaire; wants evidence pack under NDA.
- Procurement: sourcing manager will be involved if/when POC converts to paid (prefers AWS marketplace/private offer if possible).

Use case details
1) Fraud ops triage
- Inputs: alert payload + recent transaction summaries + internal case notes.
- Output: recommended disposition + rationale + next actions; wants structured output for downstream tooling.
- Work pattern: bursty during incident spikes; daytime peaks.

2) Support agent assist
- Inputs: customer ticket + account history + policy snippets.
- Output: draft response + cited policy snippets (RAG) + escalation suggestions.

Performance / SLO targets (from discovery + demo Q&A)
- Fraud triage: p95 < 250ms time-to-first-token for short prompts; overall completion under ~2.5s for typical responses (150–300 tokens).
- Support: p95 < 400ms TTFT; streaming required.
- Throughput: target 40–60 concurrent requests during peaks; expects to scale higher if rolled out to all queues.
- Cost: price-sensitive; will compare against Bedrock + self-hosted; asked for clear unit economics + levers (batching/caching/quant).

Model preferences / quality constraints
- Prefers open models for control and future portability. Mentioned interest in Llama 3.x class models and Mixtral-style MoE for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Needs: function/tool calling (or equivalent structured outputs), low hallucination rate for policy citations, and deterministic-ish behavior for fraud dispositions (repeatability matters).
- Routing/fallback: liked the concept of automatic fallback (same task, compatible model variant) when capacity constrained, but wants guardrails + auditability.

Security/compliance notes (high-signal)
- Must-have: SSO/SAML for console/admin access; RBAC; audit logs w/ export (they asked explicitly: "Can we ship logs to Splunk/S3?").
- Encryption: KMS-backed encryption at rest expected; asked about customer-managed keys vs provider-managed.
- Data retention: wants explicit retention controls and a clear statement on training ("no training on customer data" language requested; needs approved wording).
- Data residency: preference for US-only; may require region pinning and controls for DR/failover.

Competitor mentions (verbatim-ish)
- "We’re piloting Bedrock right now because procurement is easy. But latency is inconsistent at peak." 
- "We’ve used OpenAI for non-prod prototyping; can’t for prod due to policy." 
- "Our infra team thinks they can self-host vLLM; we don’t want to own GPUs if we can avoid it." 
- Also evaluating Together/other inference vendors for dedicated capacity.
